definitions.explanation: The time in September when day and night are approximately equal in length, marking the midpoint of autumn.

examples.japanese: {秋分|しゅうぶん}の{日|ひ}は{祝日|しゅくじつ}だ。
examples.english: The autumnal equinox is a national holiday.

examples.japanese: {秋分|しゅうぶん}を{過|す}ぎると、{日|ひ}が{短|みじか}くなる。
examples.english: After the autumnal equinox, the days get shorter.

examples.japanese: {秋分|しゅうぶん}の{日|ひ}は{毎年|まいとし}9{月|がつ}22{日|にち}か23{日|にち}ごろになる。
examples.english: The autumnal equinox falls around September 22nd or 23rd every year.

notes:
A compound of {秋|あき} (autumn) and {分|ぶん} (division, equinox). Refers to the astronomical event when the sun crosses the celestial equator heading south.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{秋分|しゅうぶん}の{日|ひ} (Autumnal Equinox Day) is a national holiday in Japan. It falls during {秋|あき}の{彼岸|ひがん} (the autumn equinox week), when people visit family graves, clean them, and offer おはぎ (rice balls coated in sweet bean paste).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {秋分|しゅうぶん}の{日|ひ} — Autumnal Equinox Day (national holiday)
- {秋分|しゅうぶん}{点|てん} — autumnal equinox point (astronomical term)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {春分|しゅんぶん} — vernal equinox; the spring counterpart
- {彼岸|ひがん} — equinox week; the Buddhist observance period around each equinox
